stem: Imran records the heights of three books as $14$ cm, $22$ cm, and $11$ cm. The diagram shows the display he is planning for books A, B, and C.

parts.text: Which claim about orientation fits the kind of measurement?

options.text: Use upward columns so taller books read as taller bars, matching how height is compared.
Call the finished picture a vertical-column label only, without matching display direction to height.
Read the book heights as following from the column heights he draws.
Choose the plan only because $22$ is the largest printed height.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Heights compare naturally as upward extents, so vertical columns fit the measurement; the display does not set the measured heights.

teacher.key_rationale: Heights suit upward columns. Naming only a column label substitutes a term. Reading measured heights as following from the drawn columns reverses display and data. Grabbing the largest print is surface capture.
teacher.figure_note: Added vertical columns for three book heights 14, 22, 11 cm.
